entry.title: Averaging Collusion Breaks Traceability in Personalized Neural Audio Watermarking
entry.summary:
Personalized neural audio watermarking systems embed user-specific payloads into audio to trace the user associated with a leaked or misused copy. Existing evaluations mainly assume access to a single personalized copy, but real-world distribution may expose multiple copies of the same recording. We find that simple sample-wise averaging breaks traceability: averaging only two copies produces tracing-failure rates of 87.7-99.7% across the five systems while largely preserving audio quality.

Source: arXiv Cryptography & Security (cs.CR) · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #multimodal #neuroscience
